record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: If V is an asymptotically flat spacetime with a Cauchy surface that has no horizons, must V contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?

evidence.quote: Let V be an AF spacetime, having a Cauchy surface without horizons. Show there is a maximal Cauchy hypersurface in V.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $(V,g)$ be an asymptotically flat spacetime (a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian 4-manifold whose Cauchy data on a Cauchy surface decay to those of Minkowski space at spatial infinity in a suitable weighted sense). Suppose $V$ is globally hyperbolic and admits a Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$ that contains no horizons (no points lying on the boundary of the past or future of any inextendible causal curve from infinity; equivalently, the development of $\Sigma$ has no event horizons relative to the asymptotic region). Must $V$ contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface, i.e., a smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface whose mean curvature with respect to the future-directed unit normal vanishes identically?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial existence results for maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes (notably by Bartnik and others) are known under various interior assumptions, but the general question of whether the absence of horizons on a Cauchy surface in an asymptotically flat spacetime guarantees the existence of a maximal Cauchy hypersurface appears to remain open. Surveys on global Cauchy problem and CMC/maximal foliations list closely related questions as open.

status_evidence.title: Maximal Surfaces and General Relativity (Bartnik)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses existence of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes under interior/horizon-type hypotheses; full existence under absence-of-horizons hypothesis is not established in general.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results are partial; conditions involving horizons play a central role.

status_evidence.title: Theorems on Existence and Global Dynamics for the Einstein Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Whether spacetimes admitting an asymptotically flat Cauchy surface also admit one of constant mean curvature (including maximal) is an open question.
status_evidence.claim: Related existence questions for CMC/maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces remain open.

status_evidence.title: Existence of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Bartnik proves existence of maximal surfaces under specific interior conditions in AF spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Partial existence results exist; the question of complete characterization is unresolved.
